excerpts.excerpt: Consolidating stored experience into model weights requires deciding both which experience to train on and when its external records can leave retrieval.
A verification gate then compares the updated model without episodic retrieval against the base model with retrieval on reserved probes.
Release requires valid training participation and scores meeting both relative and absolute criteria; records for skills that fail verification remain retrievable.

method_excerpts.excerpt: Memory release requires valid training participation, nonempty probes, and both relative and absolute performance conditions
Skills with no probes remain ineligible for release
with retrieval from the pre-release store
prevents memory release for a skill that contributes no valid examples
Training or loading failure leaves records and existing deployment approvals unchanged
Moving records to an archive reduces the retrievable footprint but does not reduce total retained storage
The intended unit of separation is the originating episode

method_formula.text: z = u * b * I[N > 0] * I[A_W - A_M >= delta] * I[A_W > alpha]
method_formula.mapping: u: admission; b: training participation (|D_s| > 0); N: probe count; A_W: candidate without episodic retrieval; A_M: base with retrieval; delta: margin (may be negative); alpha: strict floor

empirical_claims.note: Paper figures, recorded as found and not checked by this sketch. They appear only in this file.

claims.text: Three of five skills qualify for release
archive 331 records and leave 269 retrievable, reducing the retrievable footprint by 55.2%
QA probes use an answer-score threshold of 0.5
Release requires a score strictly above 50%
Immediate release leaves only 13 retrievable records but lowers F1 from 71.1 to 66.8

not_results_of_this_sketch: The skills, records, rules, probes and every fixture outcome are synthetic. Nothing here trains a model, touches weights, or reproduces or measures any benchmark, model, adapter or release policy studied in the paper.
